newsitem.title: USA: BPA begins sale, lease of low-voltage substations.
newsitem.headline: BPA begins sale, lease of low-voltage substations.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Thursday it has completed the first of several expected deals to sell or lease its low-voltage substations to customer utilities.
BPA is committed to selling 126 substations of 34.5 kilovolts or less to 37 customer utilities in an April 1996 agreement.
The federal power marketing agency said Thursday it has sold equipment at Parker Substation northwest of Eugene, Ore., to Blackly-Lane Electric Cooperative.

The price of the sale was not disclosed, but BPA has said earlier "prices negotiated ensure that the federal investment is fully recovered and that costs or liabilities are not shifted from one group of ratepayers to another."
BPA sent suggested prices to customers for single-customer facilities in late December and is preparing for negotiations on 18 other substations for which it has received applications.
BPA said it will offer suggested prices on the remaining facilities over the next four months.
